questions.question: In which state is the Sarhul festival celebrated?
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Sarhul is a popular festival celebrated by **various tribes in the Jharkhand region.** The festival is the tribal New Year and is celebrated by the Munda, Oraon, Ho, etc. tribes of Jharkhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is celebrated by the Oraon, the Munda, and the Ho tribes, of the Jharkhand region.
 
• Celebrated every year in the first month of the Hindu calendar, on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of 'Chaitra', Sarhul marks the advent of the spring season or “Phaagun” and is celebrated till the month of June or “Jeth”.
 
• Sarhul means worship of trees. **Being close to nature, these tribes start the Sarhul festival with the worship of trees and other elements of nature.**

questions.question: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Easter is one of the most significant festivals in Christianity, marking the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
 
• This festival is celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox.
 
• Easter is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.
 
• The Easter festival also includes traditions such as Easter eggs and the Easter Bunny, which symbolize new life and rebirth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Easter:**

 
 
• Easter is a festival and holiday commemorating the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, described in the New Testament as having occurred on the third day of his burial after his crucifixion by the Romans at Calvary c. 30 AD.
 
• It is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent (or Great Lent), a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.
 
• Most Christians refer to the week before Easter as "Holy Week"—it contains the days of the Easter Triduum, including Maundy Thursday (commemorating the Maundy and Last Supper), as well as Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion and death of Jesus).
 
• In Western Christianity, Easter is always celebrated on the Sunday following the first full moon that occurs on or after the spring equinox.
 
 
 
• **Christianity:**
 
 
• Christianity is an Abrahamic monotheistic religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth. It is the world's largest religion, with about 2.4 billion followers.
 
• Its adherents, known as Christians, believe that Jesus is the Christ, whose coming as the Messiah was prophesied in the Hebrew Bible, called the Old Testament in Christianity, and chronicled in the New Testament.
 
• Christian theology is summarized in creeds such as the Apostles' Creed and the Nicene Creed, which state that Jesus suffered, died, was buried, descended into hell, and rose from the dead, and ascended into heaven, from where he will return.
 
• Christianity is divided into three main branches: Catholicism, Orthodoxy, and Protestantism.

questions.question: Makar Sankranti is the festival dedicated to which of the following Lords?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Makar Sankranti is dedicated to the Hindu sun god, **Surya**.
 
• It is one of the few Hindu festivals that is observed according to the solar cycles, unlike other festivals which follow the lunar calendar.
 
• The festival marks the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of **Makara (Capricorn)** on its celestial path.
 
• Makar Sankranti is also known as **Uttarayan** and is celebrated with kite flying, bonfires, and feasts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Makar Sankranti**

 
 
• Makar Sankranti is a festival day in the Hindu calendar, dedicated to the deity Surya (sun).
 
• It is observed each year in January and is a significant solar event.
 
• The festival is also a cultural festival, observed by Hindus and Sikhs, and marks the end of the winter solstice and the start of longer days.
 
• Traditional practices include taking holy dips in rivers like Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery.
 
 
 
• **Surya**
 
 
• Surya is the solar deity in Hinduism.
 
• He is considered the source of life and energy, and is often depicted riding a chariot harnessed by seven horses, which represent the seven colors of light and the seven days of the week.
 
• Surya is worshipped during various festivals throughout the year, including Makar Sankranti, Pongal, and Chhath.
 
 
 
• **Other Associated Festivals**
 
 
• **Pongal** - Celebrated in Tamil Nadu, it is a four-day festival marking the harvest season and is dedicated to the sun god.
 
• **Lohri** - Celebrated in Punjab, it marks the passing of the winter solstice and is associated with the harvest of the rabi crops.
 
• **Uttarayan** - In Gujarat, Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Uttarayan and is known for the International Kite Festival.

questions.question: Which among the following festival marks the menstruation period of the Goddess Kamakhya in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ambubachi Mela.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ambubachi Mela:-**

 
 
• It is also known as Ambubasi festival or Ameti festival, is an annual religious festival celebrated in the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, India.
 
• It is one of the most important festivals in the state of Assam and attracts thousands of devotees from various parts of the country.
 
• The festival is centered around the Kamakhya Devi Temple, which is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kamakhya.
 
• According to Hindu mythology, during the festival, the goddess Kamakhya is believed to undergo her annual menstrual cycle.
 
• The temple remains closed for three days during this period as it is considered to be an impure time.
 
 
 
• **Goddess Kamakhya:-**
 
 
• It is a prominent deity in Hindu mythology, particularly in the Shakta tradition.
 
• She is revered as a powerful and fertility goddess, often associated with feminine energy and the creative force of the universe.
 
• Kamakhya is primarily worshipped in the Kamakhya Temple, located on the Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moatsu:-**

 
 
• ​It** **is a significant festival celebrated by the Ao Naga tribe in the northeastern state of Nagaland, India.
 
• It is observed in the month of May every year, specifically from the 1st to the 7th of the month.
 
 
 
• **Chapchar Kut:-**
 
 
• It is a harvest festival celebrated by the Mizos, an ethnic group predominantly found in the northeastern state of Mizoram, India, as well as in parts of Myanmar and Bangladesh.
 
• It is one of the most important festivals for the Mizo people and is usually held in March after the completion of the jhum (shifting cultivation) cycle.
 
 
 
• **Wangala:-**
 
 
• **​**Wangala is a harvest festival celebrated by the Garo tribe, which is one of the major indigenous communities in the northeastern region of India, particularly in the states of Meghalaya, Assam, and parts of Bangladesh.
 
• The festival is also known as Wangala or Drua Wanbola and is considered one of the most significant cultural events for the Garo people.

questions.question: Hareli festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hareli is a traditional agricultural festival celebrated primarily in the state of **Chhattisgarh, India**.
 
• The festival is observed in the Hindu month of **Shravan (July-August)** and marks the beginning of the agricultural season.
 
• Farmers worship farm tools, bullocks, and plows, and offer prayers to deities such as **Goddess Hareli** and **Mother Earth**.
 
• The celebrations include decorating bullocks, preparing traditional dishes, and engaging in unique local games like **Gedi (walking on bamboo stilts)**.
 
• The festival symbolizes gratitude to nature and prayers for a **good harvest, prosperity, and the well-being** of families and livestock.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Festivals in India**

 
 
• India celebrates various agriculture-related festivals reflecting its farming culture, such as **Pongal (Tamil Nadu)**, **Baisakhi (Punjab)**, **Onam (Kerala)**, and **Makar Sankranti** (across India).
 
• These festivals often signify seasonal changes and the **harvesting of crops**, emphasizing the agrarian lifestyle of the country.
 
• They promote community bonding and **preserve indigenous traditions**.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh's Cultural Heritage**
 
 
• Chhattisgarh is known as the **"Rice Bowl of India"** due to its vast paddy fields and rich agricultural practices.
 
• The state has a vibrant tribal culture, highlighted through festivals like **Bastar Dussehra**, **Madai**, and Hareli.
 
• These festivals represent **Chhattisgarh's unique cultural identity** and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Livestock in Farming**
 
 
• Livestock is crucial in traditional farming, providing **draught power, manure, and additional income** through dairy products.
 
• Festivals like Hareli emphasize the role of livestock by incorporating rituals to honor and care for animals.
 
• This practice aligns with sustainable farming techniques by integrating **animal husbandry** into agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Connection Between Festivals and Sustainability**
 
 
• Agricultural festivals like Hareli foster a deeper connection between humans and nature.
 
• They promote **sustainable farming practices** and respect for natural resources.
 
• Such celebrations encourage the sharing of **traditional knowledge** among farming communities.

questions.question: Which of the following harvest and cultural festivals is celebrated by the Tamil community every year in January?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pongal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pongal is a major harvest festival celebrated by the Tamil community in the month of January every year.
 
• The festival lasts for four days, usually from January 14th to January 17th, marking the Tamil New Year.
 
• It is named after the Tamil word "Pongal," meaning "to boil," and is celebrated with the boiling of the first rice of the season.
 
• The festival is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and signifies the end of the winter solstice and the start of the sun's six-month-long journey northwards.
 
• Pongal is celebrated with traditional rituals, including cooking a special dish called "Pongal" and offering it to the deities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhogi Pongal**

 
 
• The first day of Pongal is called Bhogi Pongal and is dedicated to Lord Indra, the god of rain.
 
• On this day, old and unwanted items are burned in a bonfire to mark the end of the old and the beginning of the new.
 
 
 
• **Surya Pongal**
 
 
• The second day, Surya Pongal, is dedicated to the Sun God and is the main day of the festival.
 
• People prepare a dish of rice, milk, and jaggery and offer it to the Sun God as a gesture of gratitude.
 
 
 
• **Mattu Pongal**
 
 
• The third day, Mattu Pongal, is dedicated to cattle (Mattu) which are considered essential for farming in Tamil culture.
 
• Cattle are decorated and worshipped, and farmers express their gratitude to them for their hard work throughout the year.
 
 
 
• **Kanum Pongal**
 
 
• The fourth day, Kanum Pongal, is a day for socializing and relaxation.
 
• Families visit relatives and friends, and various cultural events and games are organized.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Kolam**
 
 
• During Pongal, homes are decorated with beautiful Kolam (rangoli) designs made using rice flour.
 
• Kolam is believed to bring prosperity and happiness and is an integral part of the Pongal celebrations.

• The Chariot Festival, also known as Rath Yatra, is primarily celebrated in the city of Puri in Odisha, India.

• Balarama is considered a deity of agriculture and strength and is revered for his role in various Hindu epics and scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Subhadra:**

• She is worshipped as a manifestation of Goddess Durga and is believed to protect and bless her devotees.

questions.question: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shab-e-Barat is a significant Islamic observance that is celebrated by Muslims around the world.
 
• It is observed on the night between the 14th and 15th day of the Islamic month of Sha'ban.
 
• Muslims believe that on this night, God writes the destinies of all individuals for the coming year and forgives the sins of those who seek forgiveness.
 
• It is a night of prayer, reflection, and seeking forgiveness, often involving staying awake all night in devotion and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sha'ban**

 
 
• Sha'ban is the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
 
• It is considered a significant month for Muslims as it precedes the holy month of Ramadan.
 
• Many Muslims fast during this month and increase their worship in preparation for Ramadan.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Calendar**
 
 
• The Islamic calendar, also known as the Hijri calendar, is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 months in a year of 354 or 355 days.
 
• The calendar is used to determine the proper days of Islamic holidays and rituals, such as the annual period of fasting and the proper time for the pilgrimage to Mecca.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Prayer in Islam**
 
 
• Prayer, or Salah, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundation of a Muslim's faith and practice.
 
• It is a physical, mental, and spiritual act of worship that is observed five times every day at prescribed times.
